quote: Aber schon das Problem, ob zwischen abzählbar und Linearconti- nuum etwas zwischen liegt sehr schwer.
english: But already the problem whether something lies between the countable and the linear continuum is very hard.
topic: Reflecting on Cantor's letters, Hilbert considers the problem of which collections may be regarded as 'finished' (complete) in set theory, and proposes formulating set-theoretic propositions without the word 'set' and treating terms such as 'irrational number' merely as names for things with specified properties.

triage.modern_statement: Cantor's Continuum Hypothesis (CH): is there a set whose cardinality is strictly greater than that of the natural numbers (ℵ0) and strictly less than that of the real line (2^ℵ0)? Put another way, is 2^ℵ0 = ℵ1, so that every uncountable set of reals has the same size as ℝ?
triage.answered_by: This is Hilbert's 1st Problem, from his 1900 Paris list. It was settled in a metamathematical sense: CH can be neither proved nor disproved in ZFC. Kurt Gödel showed in 1938/1940 that CH is consistent with ZFC, using the constructible universe L. Paul Cohen showed in 1963 that the negation of CH is also consistent with ZFC, using forcing, which he invented for this purpose.

evidence.claim: CH says there is no cardinality strictly between ω and the cardinality of the continuum. Cantor posed it in 1878, and it was the first of Hilbert's 23 problems.
Gödel proved in 1938 that CH is consistent with ZFC. Cohen developed forcing in 1963 and used it to prove that ¬CH is consistent with ZFC, which completed the independence proof.
Settling CH was the first of Hilbert's problems presented in 1900. Its independence was proved in 1963 by Paul Cohen, building on Gödel's 1940 work.

Feferman describes how CH went from #1 on Hilbert's list to a metamathematical problem through the work of Gödel and Cohen. He also discusses whether CH is still a definite mathematical problem and whether new axioms would be needed to decide it.
Woodin's Ultimate L project, funded by the NSF, aims to find an axiom 'V = Ultimate L' that would resolve questions like CH and could not be undone by forcing.
Set theorists and philosophers still debate the prospects for CH, including Hamkins's multiverse view versus Woodin's program for proving CH true.

triage.why: The diary note asks whether anything lies between the countable and the linear continuum. That is exactly Cantor's Continuum Hypothesis, which Hilbert put first on his 1900 list. Gödel (1940) and Cohen (1963) together showed that ZFC cannot decide it. Whether CH has a definite answer under new axioms is still actively researched and debated, for example in Woodin's Ultimate L program and Hamkins's multiverse view.
